frozen_principle: FAE must remain secure even if the attacker knows 100% of the source code.

present.note: reproducible verification commands and security boundary
client-side wallet/key derivation and Ed25519 handling

attacker_model: Full source-code knowledge and arbitrary local source modification.
Arbitrary malformed blocks, transactions, protocol messages and API inputs.
Multiple adversarial peers and coordinated peer identities.
Timing, race, restart, reorg, stale-work and concurrency attacks.
Dependency, build, release and supply-chain attacks.
No security claim may depend on an honest client or hidden implementation.

allowed: non-consensus observability needed for security verification

global_invariants: Maximum supply can never be exceeded.
Invalid block reward or coinbase cannot be accepted.
A lower-work chain cannot replace a valid higher-work chain under the authoritative fork-choice rule.
Malformed external input cannot corrupt canonical state.
Crash/restart/recovery cannot create or destroy value.
Stale or abandoned work cannot mutate consensus state.
Independent conforming implementations must reach the same consensus result for the same valid input/history.
Private keys and seed phrases never enter Build Colony, CI, logs, fixtures or security evidence.
Every fixed vulnerability becomes an executable regression test when technically feasible.
Static/dependency scanners are defense-in-depth signals, never substitutes for adversarial verification.
Security claims remain fail-closed when required evidence is missing.

phases.name: Boundary Freeze and Execution Binding
phases.exit: Exact source revision, Build Colony revision, authority ceiling, attacker model, invariants and workstream termination condition are frozen in the repository.

phases.name: Formal Public-Code Threat Model
phases.exit: Threat actors, assets, trust boundaries, capabilities, exclusions and abuse classes are explicit; hidden-code and honest-client assumptions are forbidden.

phases.name: Existing Security Gate and Evidence Inventory
phases.exit: Every existing relevant test/check/workflow is mapped to the invariant it supports; gaps are evidence-bound rather than assumed.

phases.name: Attack-Surface Matrix and Invariant Registry
phases.exit: Consensus, wallet/keys, tx validation, mining/templates, P2P/discovery/eclipse, reorg/fork choice, persistence/recovery, browser/frontend, APIs/backend, and build/release/dependencies each have explicit invariants and owners.

phases.name: Responsible Disclosure Baseline
phases.exit: SECURITY.md exists with private reporting path, supported scope, disclosure expectations and no implied bounty commitment.

phases.name: Consensus and Economic Hostile Gates
phases.exit: Executable adversarial gates cover reward, supply, maturity, duplicate spend, malformed block/tx, fork choice and consensus-state invariants.

phases.name: Wallet, Keys and Signature Hostile Gates
phases.exit: Invalid-key/signature, recovery, derivation, key-material leakage and misuse cases are adversarially tested without persistent secrets.

phases.name: P2P, Discovery and Eclipse Hostile Gates
phases.exit: Malformed peers/messages, peer concentration, isolation/eclipse, stale view and reconnection abuse are covered by executable tests or explicit evidence blockers.

phases.name: Persistence, Reorg and Recovery Hostile Gates
phases.exit: Crash/restart, partial write, corrupted local state, rollback/reorg and mempool reconstruction preserve value and deterministic canonical state.

phases.name: Browser, Frontend, API and Backend Boundary Gates
phases.exit: Untrusted browser/API/backend inputs, origin/state assumptions and resource bounds are adversarially exercised without granting backend authority over keys or consensus.

phases.name: Hostile Corpus, Property Testing and Fuzzing
phases.exit: Reusable malformed corpus plus property/fuzz harnesses exercise parsers/state transitions; discovered failures are minimized and retained as regressions.

phases.name: Differential and Alternative-Implementation Verification
phases.exit: Consensus-critical cases are replayed through independent code paths/implementations where available and divergence fails closed.

phases.name: Supply-Chain and Public-Repo Hygiene
phases.exit: Dependency inventory/update policy, Dependabot candidate, CodeQL/static-analysis candidate, secret-leak prevention and least-privilege CI review are present and verified as defense in depth.

phases.name: Reproducible Build and Release Provenance
phases.exit: Build/release inputs, hashes and provenance are reproducible enough to verify that published artifacts correspond to reviewed source.

phases.name: Open-Source License Decision and Explicit License
phases.exit: MIT vs Apache-2.0 is resolved as a separate legal/project decision and an explicit license is committed; this phase does not satisfy any security gate by itself.

phases.name: Project Assurance White-Box Attack Campaign
phases.exit: Project Assurance/Red Team attacks the exact candidate assuming full source knowledge; findings are evidence-bound and severity does not get waived by passing scanners.

phases.name: Finding Closure and Regression Promotion
phases.exit: Every admitted finding is fixed, explicitly accepted as residual risk, or blocks readiness; fixes carry regression tests where feasible.

phases.name: Full Security Baseline Replay
phases.exit: Canonical verification plus all new security gates replay GREEN on the exact candidate revision with no selective retry hiding failures.

phases.name: Public-Code Security Baseline Verdict
phases.exit: Verdict is one of BASELINE_READY_FOR_RECURRING_ASSURANCE, BLOCKED_BY_SECURITY_FINDINGS, or BLOCKED_BY_MISSING_EVIDENCE; it grants no mainnet authority.

phases.name: Bounded Project Closeout and Recurring Assurance Handoff
phases.exit: Extraordinary workstream is closed; only recurring Project Assurance remains, with deeper review mandatory for consensus, crypto, economics and critical networking changes.

first_execution_block.label: Baseline Definition Block
first_execution_block.note: PSR-01 and PSR-02 may execute in parallel after PSR-00 is integrated; PSR-03 serializes their outputs. PSR-04 may proceed once PSR-01 is stable.

parallelization_policy.rule: Parallelize independent surfaces; serialize shared security contracts and integration.

termination_condition: The bounded hardening project ends after PSR-18 yields BASELINE_READY_FOR_RECURRING_ASSURANCE and PSR-19 records the handoff. No permanent new security system is created.
